checkpoint_rule: 23:32 is preserved as an observational checkpoint only; no causal, prophetic, or statistical significance is inferred from the time itself.
target_gate: Find one real Egyptian text where cloth/wrapping + oil/liquid + soaking/moistening + wringing/pressing occur in one local instruction or tightly connected procedure.

strongest_single_text_match.source: Papyrus Edwin Smith, case sequence around column 5, especially 5.12 and 5.19
strongest_single_text_match.transliteration_primary: wdi̯.ḫr=k sšm.wj.DU n(.j) ḥbs jwḥ m mrḥ.t m-ẖnw msꜣḏ.t.DU=fj
strongest_single_text_match.semantic_summary: The instruction orders two swabs/plugs made of cloth/linen, moistened with oil/fat, to be placed into the nostrils. A closely parallel instruction at 5.19 again specifies two cloth swabs moistened with oil/fat.

shared_nodes.FORM: sšm.wj = two swabs/plugs/tampons made from cloth

reverse_pattern_result.modern_core: SORPTIVE_TEXTILE_LIKE_MATERIAL + OIL_CONTACT + LIQUID_UPTAKE -> RETRIEVE -> WRING/PRESS -> RECOVER_OIL
reverse_pattern_result.remaining_missing_edge: MOISTENED_OIL_BEARING_CLOTH -> WRING/PRESS -> RECOVER_OIL IN THE SAME LOCAL PROCEDURE

scientific_boundary: The Edwin Smith instruction is a medical application of oil-moistened linen swabs, not an oil-recovery process.
The existence of sꜥrq as a wringing verb does not prove that the same oil-moistened cloth was wrung to recover oil.
No SCOBY, kombucha, bacterial-cellulose sheet, aerogel or oil-spill sorbent is identified by these texts.
next_gate: Search TLA and primary editions for a single local procedure combining ḥbs/sšr.w/mnḫ.t with jwḥ or another wetting verb, mrḥ.t/bꜣq or another oil term, and sꜥrq/nwdi̯ or another squeeze/press operator; prioritize medical, embalming, laundry, perfumery and oil-production texts.
